the intercept is exactly 100 divisions or not. If it is not, the wire diaphragm must be shifted in the tube until it is. In figs. 3, 4, 5 and 6 the distances are deduced from the readings of a central wire in the optical axis of the telescope and of a wire above it, for the sake of simplicity. The usual arrangement is to fit the diaphragm with a central wire and with one or two wires above and below it at equal distances from the central wire. The vertical angle of depression or elevation is fixed by directing the central wire to a well-defined division on the staff, and the distance of the staff is inferred from the readings given by the corresponding wires above and below the central wire.

Let <math>\text{O}</math> be the point where the vertical axis of the instrument cuts the axis of the telescope, the instrument being centred over a peg, from which the distance to the staff is required. The object glass (of focal length <math>= f</math>) is at a distance <math>c</math> from <math>\text{O}</math>. Let <math>\text{AT} = u</math> and <math>\text{AH} = v</math>, and the angle <math>\text{SAT} = \text{HAK} = \theta</math>. Then if <math>i</math> be the height of the image <math>\text{HK}</math>, <math>i = v \tan \theta</math>. Since <math>1/v + 1/u = 1/f</math>, we have <math>v = -uf/(u-f)</math>, and hence <math>i = uf \tan \theta/(u-f)</math>. Let <math>\text{F}</math> be some point on <math>\text{AT}</math> such that <math>\text{AF} = x</math> and <math>\text{FT} = u'</math>. And let the angle <math>\text{SFT} = \phi</math>. Then <math>u = u' + x</math> and <math>\tan \theta = u' \tan \phi/(u' + x)</math>, and therefore
{{block center|<math>i = \frac{(u'+x)f}{u'+x-f}\frac{u'}{u'+x}\cdot \tan \phi = \frac{fu'}{u'+x-f} \tan \phi</math>; and, if <math>x = f</math>, <math>i = f \tan \phi</math>.}}

If therefore the point <math>\text{F}</math> be taken at a distance <math>f</math> from the object glass, every intercept of the staff for positions between <math>\text{T}</math> and <math>\text{F}</math>, such as <math>\text{S}'\text{T}'</math>, <math>\text{S}''\text{T}''</math>, &c., which are bounded by the line <math>\text{FS}</math>, and for which consequently <math>\theta</math> is the same, will have the same height of image at the diaphragm. Conversely, if <math>\text{K}</math> be a wire in the diaphragm it will cut the image of the staff for all positions of the staff between <math>\text{T}</math> and <math>\text{F}</math> in points that lie on the line <math>\text{FS}</math>. Now the intercept <math>\text{S}''\text{T}''</math>, half-way between <math>\text{F}</math> and <math>\text{T}</math>, will be one-half of <math>\text{ST}</math>, and therefore if the reading on the staff indicated by the wire in question be one-half of <math>\text{ST}</math>, it may be inferred that the position of the staff is half-way between <math>\text{F}</math> and <math>\text{T}</math>, and similarly for other distances.
